questions.q: What job step type should a SQL Server Agent job use to run a deployed SSIS package?
options: SQL Server Integration Services Package
Transact-SQL Script (T-SQL)
Operating System (CmdExec) only
PowerShell, with no other option
questions.explain: The SSIS Package job step type is built specifically to run a package deployed to the SSIS Catalog, with its own Package Source and configuration options.

questions.q: Why should a SQL Server Agent job step that runs WorkOrderETL run as a dedicated proxy account rather than the Agent service account?
options: So the step has exactly the access the package needs — no more, no less — instead of whatever broader access the Agent service account happens to have
Proxy accounts run packages faster than the Agent service account
The Agent service account cannot run SSIS packages under any circumstances
It removes the need to deploy the package to SSISDB at all
questions.explain: A dedicated proxy scopes the job step's permissions to exactly what the package needs, which is also why a package that runs fine in SSDT can still fail from the job if the proxy is missing rights the developer had personally.

questions.q: Which call does a SQL Server Agent SSIS Package job step ultimately rely on to run a catalog-deployed package?
options: dtexec against the ISServer, or the catalog's own start_execution stored procedure
A direct HTTP call to the Power BI Service
bcp.exe
sqlcmd, with no other mechanism available
questions.explain: Under the hood, running a catalog-deployed package comes down to dtexec /ISServer or a direct call to catalog.start_execution.

questions.q: Where do you schedule refresh for a Power BI dataset that reads dw.FactWorkOrder?
options: On the semantic model itself, in the Power BI Service, via the Refresh menu's Schedule refresh option
Inside Power BI Desktop, using File > Publish
In SQL Server Agent, as a job step
In the SSIS catalog's environment variables
questions.explain: Scheduled refresh is configured on the semantic model in the Power BI Service, separate from the SSIS job that refreshes the warehouse underneath it.

questions.q: Why does the timing between the SSIS job's schedule and the Power BI refresh schedule matter?
options: The warehouse needs to finish refreshing before Power BI's scheduled refresh runs, or the dashboard will refresh against stale or incomplete data
Power BI refuses to refresh on the same day an SSIS job has run
SQL Server Agent and Power BI schedules must always use the exact same time slot
There is no relationship between the two schedules
questions.explain: Because Power BI reads the same warehouse tables the SSIS job populates, its refresh needs to be scheduled comfortably after the SSIS job's usual finish time.
